title: Bramley and rhubarb compote with oat crunch

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Apples, rhubarb, orange, sugar, golden syrup, oats, seeds, nuts and oil are all plain cupboard or garden foods.

supermarket.reason: Bramleys, forced rhubarb, oranges, oats, pumpkin seeds and hazelnuts are all everyday items at a mainstream UK supermarket in February.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a lidded saucepan and a frying pan, and the techniques are simple stewing and toasting.

works.reason: About a kilo of fruit stewed in its own juice and the orange juice, plus about 170g of toasted crunch, gives a sensible breakfast for four, sweetened enough by the sugar and syrup.

honest_times.reason: Peeling and chopping three Bramleys, cutting the rhubarb, zesting the orange and chopping the nuts fits in 15 minutes, and 12 minutes of stewing matches the steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and the cinnamon appear in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm Bramley compote with early forced rhubarb suits a February morning, and the apple is clearly the base of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Stewed fruit with oats, seeds and nuts is a real-food breakfast with modest added sugar that a family would happily eat again.
